# Serverless Analytics Dashboard  
A real-time data visualization platform built with serverless architecture, designed for scalable, low-latency analytics pipelines. This project demonstrates how to leverage event-driven compute and distributed systems to deliver actionable insights without managing infrastructure.  

## Testing  
Automated testing is central to this project. Unit tests for core logic are written in Jest, while integration tests validate end-to-end workflows using Cypress. GitHub Actions runs a full test suite on every push, ensuring 95%+ code coverage. Stress tests simulate 10,000 concurrent data ingestion requests to validate latency thresholds.  

## Getting Started / Installation  
1. Clone the repository using `git clone https://github.com/your-username/serverless-analytics-dashboard.git`  
2. Install dependencies with `npm install`  
3. Configure environment variables for AWS Lambda and DynamoDB in `.env.local`  
4. Deploy with the provided CloudFormation template or Serverless Framework CLI  

## Usage / Examples  
Launch the dashboard via `npm run start` to view real-time metrics. Example use cases:  
- Monitor user engagement with 1-second latency updates  
- Trigger alerts when query performance degrades by >20%  
- Export aggregated data to S3 buckets for downstream analysis  

## Tech Stack  
- Backend: AWS Lambda (Node.js 18), DynamoDB, API Gateway  
- Frontend: React with Chart.js for visualization  
- Data Pipelines: Apache Kafka for event streaming  
- CI/CD: GitHub Actions with Terraform for infrastructure-as-code  

## Architecture / Design  
The system uses a publish-subscribe model: Kafka producers send analytics events to Lambda workers, which process data and update DynamoDB. The frontend subscribes to S3 bucket events for real-time updates. All components are stateless, enabling horizontal scaling. Monitoring is handled via CloudWatch metrics and custom dashboards.
